newsitem.title: CANADA: Ecology suit over Canadian reactor sale to China.
newsitem.headline: Ecology suit over Canadian reactor sale to China.

text.p: Canadian ecologists said on Monday they would sue the Canadian government over its planned sale of two huge nuclear reactors to China.

"The planned lawsuit will charge that the government is violating its own environmental laws to promote the interests of the nuclear industry," the Sierra Club of Canada and Energy Probe announced in a statement.

The groups called a news conference for Tuesday, the same day that Prime Minister Jean Chretien is to preside over the signing of the agreement in Shanghai for two Candu-6 reactors at a cost of C$4.5 billion ($3.4 billion).
"On November 6th, a special cabinet meeting passed a regulation undermining the Canadian Environmental Assessment Act and its application to projects outside Canada," the statement said.
"The impetus for this new regulation was to avoid public involvement in an environmental assessment of Canada's nuclear exports to China," it said.
Chretien's office said it had no comment at the moment.
The reactors, each with a capacity of 700 megawatts, are to be built by the government's Atomic Energy of Canada Ltd.
